title: PowerShell C2 Beacon on WORKSTATION5
summary: User pgustavo's powershell.exe on WORKSTATION5 established 35 connections to external IP 10.10.10.5:80, which is a private address not in company network ranges -- consistent with C2 beaconing over HTTP/S. The destination IP's suspicious reputation and the high volume of connections confirm malicious command-and-control activity.
evidence: powershell.exe on WORKSTATION5 (user pgustavo) connected to 10.10.10.5:80 with 35 connections
IP 10.10.10.5 rated suspicious -- private address not in company known ranges
User pgustavo is a Domain lab user with WORKSTATION5 as normal host
MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001 confirmed: Application Layer Protocol Web Protocols C2 over HTTP/S

title: LSASS Memory Dumping via PowerShell on WORKSTATION5
summary: PowerShell.exe on WORKSTATION5 opened lsass.exe with memory-read access (0x1010), consistent with credential dumping. This is part of the same attack chain as the prior ALERT-001 PowerShell C2 beacon on the same host. The user pgustavo (Domain user, lab) launched whoami.exe via PowerShell at 14:32:47, followed by lsass memory access at 14:32:57.
evidence: powershell.exe opened lsass.exe with 0x1010 memory-read access per ALERT-002
whoami.exe launched by powershell.exe at 14:32:47 as child process under user pgustavo
user pgustavo is a Domain user (lab) with WORKSTATION5 as normal host
MITRE confirmation: T1003.001 (OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory) and T1059.001 (PowerShell execution)
prior finding ALERT-001: PowerShell C2 Beacon on WORKSTATION5 (true_positive) indicates ongoing attack
related_to_prior: Same host WORKSTATION5; continues the attack chain from ALERT-001 PowerShell C2 Beacon - attacker using PowerShell for credential dumping after initial compromise

recommended_actions.action: Preserve forensic memory dump of WORKSTATION5 for analysis
Reset credentials for user pgustavo and any accounts that may have been exposed
Enable LSA Protection/Credential Guard if not already active
Review PowerShell script block logging and AMSI logs for additional indicators
